paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities of clinically relevant tokens for the MistralV0.2-Base model and its variants fine-tuned on six medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The x-axis displays these six specialty groups, arranged in order from left to right, while the y-axis represents negative log probability on a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 to -22, with tick marks at intervals of 1 unit. Within each specialty group, there are seven vertical bars: the light blue bar represents the baseline MistralV0.2-Base model, and the six colored bars (light orange to dark brown) represent models fine-tuned on each of the six specialties, as indicated by the legend. The baseline model consistently exhibits the highest (least negative) negative log-probability values across all specialties, with values around -23.5 for Infect and approximately -22.5 for Cardio, indicating weaker token prediction performance. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant consistently achieves the lowest (most negative) negative log-probability values across all specialty groups, suggesting strong generalization or cross-specialty transfer. The Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with the baseline reaching approximately -23.5 and the fine-tuned models ranging down to about -25.5. In contrast, the Cardio group displays the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned models, with a difference of roughly 1.5 units. The bars are grouped by specialty, and each group contains the same set of models, allowing direct comparison of performance improvements across fine-tuning strategies within each specialty. No bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding, and the chart does not include error bars or statistical annotations.
